name: Lathami Conservation Park
reason: Official SA government page says the park is closed for public safety after the 2020 bushfires (glossy black-cockatoo habitat); no confirmed reopening, no visitor facilities named.

name: Kangaroo Island Shipwreck Trail

Case against: a dispersed set of roadside/shore signs (e.g. Kona wreck at Antechamber Bay), no single place to spend half an hour; individual sites are the places.

name: Cape St Albans

name: Kangaroo Island
reason: Duplicate of the island itself (parent destination), not a spot.

name: The Cliffs Kangaroo Island
reason: Golf course / shore-excursion operator, a business not a sightseeing place.

name: Emu Bay Lavender Farm
reason: Producer with gift shop; a business, not a distinct visitor attraction.

name: Waterfall Creek Hike (Flinders Chase)
reason: Named DOC-style walk in Flinders Chase on the tourism board page: trail down to a creek, stepping stones and a lookout over a seasonal waterfall, from the Western River car park on Colmans Rd. Distinct walk; worth an hour. Seasonal waterfall.

name: Return Road Hike (Flinders Chase)
reason: Named walk on the tourism board page: lightkeepers' old cart track between Harveys Return and Cape Borda through sugar gum woodland past the lightkeepers' cemetery, can extend to the Clifftop lookout. Hours-long distinct walk.

name: Harveys Return Hike (Flinders Chase)
reason: Named walk on the tourism board page following the lightkeepers' original route toward Cape Borda with ocean views; steep sections. Distinct walk; overlaps partly with Return Road Hike (same corridor) but is its own named route. Flinders Chase page on parks.sa.gov.au is the managing agency.

name: Penneshaw Beach
reason: Tourism board names this 600 m town beach (Hog Bay) with picnic facilities, a swim and a monument to the French explorers; a harbour-town beach is a second-tier stop. Only one counted source and a short visit but beaches a guide names are kept.

name: Red Banks Beach
reason: Tourism board names the colourful red-orange cliffs 15 min north of American River, best at sunset; a second-tier scenic stop. Minimal facilities.

name: Hanson Bay Wildlife Sanctuary
reason: Private cabin accommodation and operator; the Koala Walk is by pre-booked guided tour only. Business, not open freely to the public.

name: Nepean Bay Beach
reason: Tourism board entry describes only a narrow, steep beach backed by dense vegetation with history of naming; nothing to see or do named, and it is a long bay rather than a distinct stop.

name: Point Ellen
reason: Tourism board names the Vivonne Bay western headland for coastal scenery, crashing Southern Ocean waves and turquoise rock pools to swim in (swell warning). Second-tier headland a guide names.

name: Penneshaw Market
reason: Periodic village market (not an every-day venue); events/markets are not spots.

name: Old Mulberry Tree
reason: Duplicate of Reeves Point (Kingscote), where Wikivoyage places the lookout and tree; the tree is a 10-minute look, a minor heritage item propped on cables.

name: Fine Art Kangaroo Island
reason: Art gallery/shop run by an operator; a business, no distinct attraction.

name: Fireball Bates Walking Trail
reason: Tourism board names a 3 km easy interpretive loop (1-2 hours) from the visitor centre in Penneshaw to near the ferry, with signs on settler George Bates. Named walk.

name: Flour Cask Bay Beach
reason: Tourism board says swimming is unsafe, access difficult, little development; nothing for a visitor to do beyond a remote surf/rip beach. Part of D'Estrees Bay shoreline.

name: Frenchmans Rock
reason: Tourism board names the rock inscribed by Baudin's crew in 1803 at Penneshaw, an historic monument; short stop but a named historic landmark. Close to Penneshaw Beach (monument at eastern end), so a modest one.
